name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 18-point Democratic lean anchors the race
Latimer is an established incumbent with a clear fundraising edge
Cinquemani shows no reported fundraising or visible campaign activity
Prediction markets price Latimer near 96 percent
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Latimer's incumbency and financial advantage, and a challenger with no visible campaign all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at roughly 96 percent. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the seat stays firmly in the safe column.
model.watch: Any sudden Republican spending, outside-group engagement, or polling showing Cinquemani within single digits would be the first sign the race is closer than its fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-16 sits in Westchester County and leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 18 points. George Latimer, a first-term incumbent with a long record in county and state government, holds the seat after a high-profile 2024 primary win. Republican Joseph Cinquemani enters as a largely unknown challenger with no reported fundraising or outside spending, and no independent polls of the race have surfaced.

Prediction markets price Latimer's chances near 96 percent, consistent with the district's fundamentals and his financial edge. With no competitive threat in the Democratic column and minimal visible Republican activity, the race lacks the ingredients typically associated with an upset. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves turnout and challenger visibility as the only plausible swing factors in an otherwise lopsided contest.
